questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive form.

Who took Bruno for a walk?

options.text: By whom has Bruno been taken for a walk?
With whom Bruno is taken for a walk?
By whom was Bruno taken for a walk?
By whom will Bruno be taken for a walk?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Who took Bruno for a walk?"
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "Bruno" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "took" to "was taken" (past simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "who" (converted to "by whom").

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"By whom was Bruno taken for a walk?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "By whom has Bruno been taken for a walk?" – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
 
• **Option 2:** "With whom Bruno is taken for a walk?" – Incorrect structure and preposition.
 
• **Option 4:** "By whom will Bruno be taken for a walk?" – Incorrect tense (future simple passive).

The error lies in part D – “the thought of it ever for” is grammatically incorrect.

 
 
• 
 
The expression “ever for” is not used in English. The word “ever” is generally used with “since” or “after” to express continuity of time from a particular event in the past up to the present.

 
 
•

• 
 
The sentence talks about a lasting emotional reaction — the speaker has continued to shiver whenever they think of the accident. To show this continued effect, the present perfect tense (“I have shivered”) must be followed by a phrase indicating continuity, i.e., “ever since.”

 
 
• 
 
Hence, the correct sentence will be:

 “That accident happened a long time ago, but I have shivered at the thought of it ever since.”

 
 
• 
 
This corrected version expresses that even though the accident occurred long ago, its emotional impact still remains with the speaker.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“That accident happened a long time ago, but I have shivered at the thought of it ever since.”*
